package.title: Tirzepatide Hair Shedding: More Common in Women #shorts
package.description:
Tirzepatide hair shedding shows up more in women than men in pooled Zepbound trials of adults with overweight or obesity: women 7.1% vs 1.3% on placebo, men 0.5% vs 0%. Why women? Not established.
See a doctor if it lasts over 6 months, is patchy, or hurts. Don't stop it on your own.
Sources: Zepbound Prescribing Information (Lilly, revised Aug 2026); American Academy of Dermatology, hair shedding.
#tirzepatide #hairloss #GLP1
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
I checked the claims against sources and they're accurate and safe. The live DailyMed Zepbound label (Revised 8/2026, section 6.1) says hair loss was reported more often in women than men on Zepbound (7.1% vs 0.5%) and on placebo (1.3% vs 0%). It also says the hair loss was "associated with weight reduction". The pooled Studies 1 and 2 enrolled adults with obesity or overweight, some of whom had type 2 diabetes, so "adults with overweight or obesity" is the right population.

On my fetch, DailyMed's adverse-reaction table only gave rounded per-dose figures (placebo 1%, 5 mg 5%, 10 mg 4%, 15 mg 5%). The overall 5.4% vs 0.9% on the s3 card matches the channel's verified key numbers and fits those per-dose values.

The AAD page supports the relief line: shedding after losing 20 pounds or more is temporary, and hair "tends to regain" its fullness within 6–9 months. DermNet lists weight loss as a trigger of telogen effluvium and says it usually corrects itself. DermNet also covers chronic cases, which makes "often temporary" correctly hedged and supports the 6-month see-a-doctor point.

The safety lines are in the right order and appear both in the narration and on screen. The Exp F and closing lines are word for word. I recounted the words: 118, inside the tight arm. Nothing advises stopping the medicine, and nothing shames anyone.

There are 2 minor wording issues, listed below. The Lilly PI PDF URL resolves but couldn't be read as text, so I've listed it as reachable, with DailyMed as the copy I actually read.

issues.fix: Men: zero point five percent, versus zero. Pooled Zepbound trials, adults with overweight or obesity. (This adds 1 word, for a total of 119, still in the tight arm.)

notes: Caption reads 'SEVEN POINT ONE PERCENT.' spelling out the number with POINT instead of matching the on-screen stat '7.1%' exactly — a banned pattern.
Mismatch between the stat pill (digits) and caption (words) breaks the 1-second readability rule since viewers see two different number formats.
Caption 'BRUSH IS UNSETTLING.' has no visual reference to a brush or hair — the scene shows a smiling pill mascot and a child icon, so the caption doesn't match what's on screen.
Captions 'MEN? ZERO POINT FIVE PERCENT.' and the general pattern spell out the number with POINT instead of matching the stat pill '0.5%' — banned pattern repeated from shot 2.
First caption ends on 'POOLED', separating it from its noun 'trials' that appears to be dropped entirely — reads as an orphaned fragment.
Generic bar chart with floating head icons feels like clip art with no clear focal character.
Scene is a near-empty room with a plain document and no character — exactly the flat document/room beat flagged as a recurring empty-shot problem.
Caption 'HAIR LOSS WITH WEIGHT REDUCTION.' has nothing visual connecting hair loss to weight loss.
Caption splits the compound idea 'weight loss' across two cards ('...FROM WEIGHT' / 'LOSS IS OFTEN...'), which reads like a broken sentence.
Speech bubble 'Often just a phase.' and the caption run at the same time as two separate text blocks, close to colliding.
Large speech bubble is completely empty — a ghost bubble with no text, which is explicitly flagged as something to delete.
Caption ends on the preposition 'ABOUT', a banned card-ending word, making it read as an unfinished sentence.
First caption ends on 'THE' ('TIRZEPATIDE QUESTION FROM THE'), a banned card-ending word and the exact Exp F line break flagged repeatedly in QA notes.
Speech bubble 'See you tomorrow!' implies a daily/dated cadence, in tension with keeping Shorts evergreen.
A small calendar icon is partially cut off at the bottom edge of the frame.
